metadata.case_name: ORLA GILROY v. EASY UP INVESTMENTS LTD

source: The Plaintiff was also treated by neurologist for post concussion syndrome.

injuries.description: Permanent nerve damage resulting in numbness and loss of sensation over right upper jaw / teeth and gums
source: (v) a molar tooth in her right upper jaw was broken and she lost sensation over the right side of her teeth and gums;
The broken tooth of the Plaintiff was removed and filled with a cap. The feeling of numbness persisted in her right upper jaw and gum and the same was likely to be permanent.

According to the report of Dr. Chan Kwan Hon, the neurologist attending the Plaintiff, dated 17th January 2006 (mistyped as 17th December 2006), the resulting numbness and loss of sensation resulted from permanent nerve damage. There is no chance of recovery. The degree of permanent disability as a result of the injury is five percent.

injuries.description: Broken molar tooth (right upper jaw) which was removed and capped

manifestations.description: Fuzziness or cloudiness in the right side of her head
Concentration not as good as before
Lost sensation over the right side of her teeth and gums
Sometimes felt like being pinched with pins and needles in her upper right lip and upper right gum area; sharp electric shock-like pain when touched (e.g. when kissing her fianc�e9e)
Right side of her face less sensitive and relatively 'dull' compared to her left side
Vomiting for the first 3 days in hospital requiring medication to control
Minor abrasions and cuts on face and body
Fear of staircases (mentioned only in court)
Severe swelling and bruising of the right side of face and head; bruising to nose and right upper lip; 10 cm bruise on right hip

treatments_received: sent to Accident & Emergency Department of Queen Mary Hospital
transferred to Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital and admitted as an inpatient
treatment by neurologist for post concussion syndrome
treatments_future: purchase of drugs for symptomatic relief

Her concentration was not as good as before.

comparable_cases.case_name: Pang Wai Hung v. MPC Express Services Company
comparable_cases.injury_description: Victim fell, hit his face on the ground and as a result lost 4 teeth with 2 other teeth chipped. Another tooth suffered pulpal death. There was also laceration on the lower chin which subsequently healed and there was a scar which is noticeable at close distance.

comparable_cases.case_name: Cheung Lap Yan and Another v. Siu Ching Kee and Another
comparable_cases.injury_description: Woman victim had 4 teeth with fracture crowns and 2 had cracked crowns. Two teeth were extracted and reconstructed with porcelain crowns. She also suffered injuries.

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Siu Sham v. Tsang Hin Sum
comparable_cases.injury_description: Victim suffered injury to head, arm and leg as a result of being assaulted by knife including 8 cm deep laceration over the vertex; post-concussional syndrome with headaches, dizziness, fatigue, irritability, difficulty in concentrating and impaired memory.

comparable_cases.case_name: Cheng Lai Kwan v. Nan Fong Textiles Ltd.

comparable_cases.case_name: So Sau Man v. Leung Ming Kwong and Another
comparable_cases.injury_description: Victim suffered right lip laceration and lost 3 teeth as a result of a traffic accident; numbness in wound area and a small scar near upper right lip; teeth were replaced by artificial ones; suturing and re-suturing due to infection.
